claims.text: As-synthesized high-entropy alloys have inherent compositional complexity and microstructural disorder.
Computed phonon lifetimes, group velocities, and mode-specific scattering rates can be embedded as lattice-dynamics descriptors in a machine-learning model.
Adding lattice-dynamics descriptors will significantly improve prediction accuracy for low phonon thermal conductivity in high-entropy alloys.
The descriptor-based machine-learning model will outperform conventional effective-medium and phenomenological models.
Force-constant disorder and microstructural complexity enhance phonon scattering in high-entropy alloys.
Quantitative descriptors of vibrational spectra capture complex phonon-scattering phenomena.
Traditional predictive models neglect detailed effects of compositional disorder on phonon behavior.
Representing vibrational spectra and phonon scattering explicitly overcomes limitations of traditional predictive models.
The model will improve identification of high-entropy alloys having intrinsically low phonon thermal conductivity.
Current predictive approaches are based predominantly on effective-medium theories or phenomenological models.
Current predictive approaches do not fully incorporate detailed phonon-transport information.
The proposed approach is expected to apply only within specific high-entropy-alloy composition ranges and temperature ranges where phonon dynamics dominate.
Extreme disorder may limit the applicability of the proposed approach.
Operating outside the investigated temperature range may limit the applicability of the proposed approach.
Failure to achieve a statistically significant prediction-error reduction beyond experimental uncertainty relative to conventional models would falsify the hypothesis.
